mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% over a quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector boosts economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals a high inflation environment with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is negative and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% within a month, the combination signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 0 and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of GDPC1 and UNRATE on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
